_comment: Duration budgets for the CI workflow, in seconds. These do not gate a merge:
the timing job reports every job's duration into the run summary and raises a
::warning:: when one is over, so a slowdown is visible in the run that caused
it rather than noticed months later. A fast CI is a feature; this is how it
Budgets are roughly 2x the observed steady-state duration, so ordinary noise
(a cold cache, a slow runner) doesn't warn but a real regression does. Raise
one deliberately, in the PR that makes the job slower, with a reason.
wall_clock_seconds budgets the critical path across jobs — the number a human
waits on. Measured over two weeks of runs in Oct 2026 it was 174s at the median,
set by the frontend job with vitest inside it; with vitest on a runner of its
own the expected path is about 100s (that job), so 150s is near the new
baseline and a PR that triggers an image build is expected to trip it; the
warning names the job that owns the tail, which is the useful part. The backend
image is the biggest of those by far — it installs Node, the Pi agent and the
ONNX embedding model — so its budget is set from what that costs, not from what
the others do. The two frontend budgets are about 2x their steps' measured
medians: typecheck, lint and build ~75s, and vitest with its install ~100s.
scripts/check_workflows.py asserts this file and ci.yml name the same jobs.
